parsed.explanation: 0.52: parent/national protections do not offset documented custody/care exposures. No criminalisation, entry restriction, facility ban, or targeted violence is documented. If a visitor is outed, risk concentrates in detention/hospital interactions: legal-sex placement, serious violations, delayed specialist care, and minor/guardian burden. Local stigma is social friction rather than organised targeting. Thin border data is not proof of safety, so Elevated Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: No trans-specific border screening, marker rejection or X-marker practice is documented. Absence of local rules is suggestive but not proof; parent border behaviour for visitors is untested.
entry_documents.protection: Parent civil/criminal law applies; no local entry restriction or gender-presentation offence is identified.
entry_documents.interaction: Any passport, ID or ticket issue would combine parent screening with local isolation; unresolved X-marker recognition is an open question.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Detention follows parent framework. Trans women legally male are placed in all-male facilities; 2021 mechanism reports serious rights violations persisting, citing ~40 transgender detainee referrals.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Parent law decriminalises trans people, bans discrimination and aggravates transphobic crimes; formal oversight and courts exist.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor, detained companion or minor could inherit birth-sex placement; oversight findings show practice may not improve through remedy.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No documented bathroom or service exclusion laws, but detention facilities use legal sex, and care facilities locally lack specialists.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Parent equality law covers housing, services and employment; marriage/partnership recognition supports visitors in family settings.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National facility law reaches locally; informal religious norms and small communities may make access ambiguous, but no specific ban is documented.

care_services.exposure: No local specialists; 2022 report found delayed access, inequity and weak self-determination. Minors face stalled transition-ban uncertainty and consent/documentation hurdles.
care_services.protection: Parent health law, national insurance coverage, lawful surgeries, and late-2024 paediatric guidelines support care.
care_services.interaction: Local isolation converts protections into travel and disclosure burdens; emergencies can out adults or minors to clinicians/guardians.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No state threat-framing or targeted harassment documented; local religious/cultural stigma, concealment and gender-variant roles coexisting with stigma are documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Parent law prohibits discrimination, criminalises conversion therapy and treats transphobia as aggravating.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Formal deterrence exists, but unremedied custody violations and unknown local enforcement reduce reliability.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minors or adults travelling with trans minors face specialist absence, travel, consent checks and policy uncertainty; guardians may be compelled to disclose documents or history.
minors_guardians.protection: Parent guidelines support blockers; national law permits care and recognizes families/marriages.
minors_guardians.interaction: Local isolation and medical caution create practical friction; a minor's care request can become an outing event.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Trans-specific street violence or police extortion is not documented; social staring/misgendering is possible from stigma.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Parent hate-crime and equality law nominally protect visitors; formal complaint channels exist.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Reporting would enter institutions with custody failures; small isolated communities may add witness and retaliation uncertainty.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Persistent detention violations lack shown remedy; care access, border practice, local enforcement, non-binary markers, and minor-ban application are unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts, preventive mechanism, equality law and criminal protections are documented nationally.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Visitor short-stay, travel distance, language and consent may make recourse too slow or expose identity further.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar birth-sex custody severity, but 0.25-C also criminalises cross-dressing and documents frequent assaults; this dossier has parent non-criminalisation, anti-discrimination law and no documented sweeps, so it is materially safer.

0.55-C has document-driven hospital placements and uneven denial. This dossier adds legal-sex custody placement, serious violations and specialist care gaps; border routine is less documented, but custody/care severity puts it slightly below 0.55-C.

0.65-A’s equality law produced release, complaint and remedy after brief detention. Here custody violations persist despite oversight and care access is poor, making the operative institutional exposure greater than 0.65-A.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: strong metropolitan rights law plus local isolation. The operative threat is institutional contact, not prosecution. Custody uses legal sex and oversight shows abuse; care is nationally protected but locally thin. For adults alone, everyday exposure seems limited; for anyone needing security, health, or care as a minor/guardian, discovery can produce humiliation, delay, or serious rights violations. No state campaign, no death penalty; social acceptance constrained.
